question: The lines $\vec{r}=(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k})+\lambda(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k})$ and $\vec{r}=(3\hat{i}+\hat{j})+\mu(4\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+4\hat{k})$ are parallel. Find the shortest distance between them.
explanation:
Step 1: Verification of parallel directions
The direction vectors are
$$\vec{b}_1=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k},\quad \vec{b}_2=4\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+4\hat{k}=2\vec{b}_1.$$
Hence, the two lines are parallel.
Step 2: Vector joining points on the lines
Taking $\vec{a}_1=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ and $\vec{a}_2=3\hat{i}+\hat{j}$,
$$\vec{a}_2-\vec{a}_1=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}.$$
Step 3: Shortest-distance relation
For parallel lines,
$$d=\frac{|\vec{b}_1\times(\vec{a}_2-\vec{a}_1)|}{|\vec{b}_1|}.$$
Step 4: Vector product and magnitudes
$$\vec{b}_1\times(\vec{a}_2-\vec{a}_1)=\hat{i}+2\hat{j},$$
so its magnitude is $\sqrt{5}$, while
$$|\vec{b}_1|=\sqrt{4+1+4}=3.$$
Step 5: Final result
Therefore,
$$d=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}$$
unit.
